subject: ACME Renewal: parachute price-hold & step-up amendment
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeretail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Renew + expand request — pricing/credits question

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the QBR last week. ACME is ready to move forward on renewal but we need to expand capacity — estimated 2.2x average monthly tokens — and we want a predictable unit price for the first 9–12 months while we re-architect.

Can Redwood provide:
- A 12-month price-hold on the current committed rate (or a step-down schedule)
- Temporary onboarding / performance credits to cover the first-month uplift surge
- Clear commit thresholds so we can plan true-ups without surprise overages

We have an internal procurement window closing 5/21 and would prefer a short amendment + DocuSign. Attached is a one-pager summary of our projected usage and timing (ACME_RFP_summary.pdf).

Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement — ACME Retail

procurement@acmeretail.com

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renew + expand request — pricing/credits question

Samantha — great to hear ACME is ready to scale. Appreciate the summary.

High level options we can move quickly on:

Option A — Committed step-up (recommended for predictability)
- Commit to 2.0x baseline for 12 months with an 18% blended discount off list for committed tokens
- Onboarding credit: $25k applied across first two invoices to offset surge
- Quarterly true-up with 10% overage buffer before higher tier pricing applies

Option B — Short price-hold + flexible burst (faster to sign)
- 9-month price-hold at current committed rate, month-to-month thereafter with 30-day notice
- One-time onboarding credit: $15k
- Burst capacity available with pay-as-you-go at a slightly elevated rate (useful for spikes)

Notes:
- We can put either option into an amendment and execute via DocuSign quickly. If procurement needs a calendar guarantee, Option A gives the clearest economics.
- I’ve looped Kar by cc to confirm finance and billing mechanics. Attaching a draft term sheet to speed review.

Next step: quick 25-minute call today or tomorrow to align and finalize which option to put in an amendment.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachment: proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Renew + expand request — pricing/credits question

Markus — quick finance check before we lock Option A numbers.

We can support Option A but would recommend tightening the onboarding credit to $20k (spread over two invoices) and capping the 10% overage buffer to 6% given ACME's predictable traffic history. If they insist on 12-month absolute price-hold without step-downs, we need to reduce the blended discount to 16% to preserve margin.

Ask: Can you confirm if ACME will commit to a minimum 2.0x calculated on trailing 3-month baseline? If yes, I approve the $20k credit and 16% discount. If they want the full 12-month flat-rate with no step changes, route to revenue leadership for sign-off.

Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmeretail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2027-05-17T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renew + expand request — pricing/credits question

Thanks Markus — this is helpful. ACME prefers the faster path to sign. We are inclined to take Option B if Redwood can extend the price-hold to 9 months (instead of 6) and increase the onboarding credit to $18k. The team also requests an explicit clause that burst capacity during month 1 will not trigger penalty pricing if usage returns to baseline within 45 days.

We can execute an amendment this week provided those two items are in the doc. Procurement deadline is 5/21.

Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement — ACME Retail
